storage: Positive integer width and height with exactly width * height signed int32 segment identifiers in row-major order. Construction copies the caller's array.

api.floodFill: map.floodFill(seed, replacement) mutates the connected region containing the row-major seed index. It returns undefined, matching the original core operation.
api.toJSON: Returns { width, height, segments } with an independent array suitable for CLI input or persistence.

fill_behavior: Use the segment identifier at the seed as the source identifier.
Replace only pixels with that identifier connected through horizontal or vertical edges.
Do not cross a row boundary or connect through a diagonal contact.
Reject an out-of-range seed or a replacement equal to the source identifier before changing the map.
Accept the full signed int32 segment range. Segment identifiers are not palette colors.

cli.input: A JSON pixel map with width, height, segments.
cli.output: The complete edited map as JSON on stdout. Errors go to stderr with exit status 1 and no partial JSON.
cli.side_effects: No file writes. A caller can redirect stdout to save the edited map.

reference.directions: 0x472cf4..0x472cff initialize right=1, down=width, left=-1; the following initialization supplies up=-width.
reference.probe: Original integer scanline instructions run on the Windows x86 host. Only calls to the deque container are redirected to a bounded in-memory deque; seven absolute direction operands are relocated. No GUI or original DLL is loaded.
reference.limits: Covers the core map mutation. Palette lookup, document history, GUI gestures, recomputation, and zap/pencil tools remain separate unresolved behavior.
